document_summary: LAHD webpage describing the City of Los Angeles Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO), with a section on California's AB 1482 statewide rent cap, as of September 2026.

rules.title: Los Angeles Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not terminate covered tenancies without just cause and must pay relocation assistance for no-fault evictions. At-fault reasons include nonpayment, uncured lease violations, nuisance or damage, and illegal use. No-fault reasons include owner or family move-in, demolition or removal from the rental market, and government vacate orders.
rules.key_value: Eviction only for listed at-fault or no-fault just causes; relocation assistance owed for no-fault evictions
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential properties in the City of Los Angeles not regulated by the RSO. Applies once the tenant has lived in the unit at least six months or the original lease has expired, whichever comes first. Can apply to buildings newer than October 1, 1978 and to a property with only one single-family dwelling.
rules.exemptions: Transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity or sorority houses, owner's roommate, certain cooperatives, some non-profit homeless facilities or short-term substance-abuse treatment centers, and some HACLA or government-owned properties.
rules.interaction: Applies to units not covered by the City's RSO, which has its own just cause rules. The JCO does not regulate rent increases; state AB 1482 may cap rent for covered units.
rules.citation: L.A. Mun. Code § 165.00 et seq. (Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance)
rules.quoted_span: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.
rules.extraction_notes: The page does not state the JCO's original effective date or the relocation amounts, so effective_date is null. Related items on the page: effective March 27, 2023, no eviction for nonpayment unless the amount owed exceeds Fair Market Rent; eviction notices must be filed with LAHD within 3 business days; a Notice of Right to Counsel must be posted from August 20, 2025. The LAMC citation is inferred from general knowledge, not from the page.}

rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act of 2019 (AB 1482) rent cap
rules.requirement: Annual rent increases on covered units are capped at 5% plus the regional change in cost of living, or 10%, whichever is lower.
rules.coverage_conditions: Buildings older than 15 years, on a rolling basis. A unit built January 1, 2006 is covered on and after January 1, 2021.
rules.exemptions: Units built within the last 15 years; deed-restricted affordable units; certain dormitories; a two-unit property where the owner occupied the second unit for the entire tenancy; qualifying single-family homes and condos not owned by a real estate trust, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member, where the tenant received the required written notice; units already subject to the City's RSO.
rules.interaction: The page says the LA JCO does not regulate rent increases, so AB 1482 may apply to JCO units. Units under the City's RSO are excluded from AB 1482 on this page.
rules.quoted_span: rent increases are limited to no more than 5% plus the percentage change in the cost of living for the region in which the property is located, or 10% whichever is lower
rules.extraction_notes: This is a secondary summary of state law on an LA city page. The page's stated maximum allowable increases are stale (8.9% for August 2024 to July 2025; 8.8% for 2023-24). The page gives no operative date for AB 1482, so effective_date is null.
